newsitem.title: USA: Boeing sued by Peru crash victims' families.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sued by Peru crash victims' families.

text.p: MIAMI, June 17, - Families of 28 victims of AeroPeru Flight 603, which crashed off the coast of Peru on October 2, 1996 killing 61 passengers and nine crew members, filed a products liability action in U.S. District Court in Miami against Boeing Co, lawyers for the plaintiff said Tuesday.

The complaint alleges that multiple design defects in Boeing's 757-200 aircraft sensor and computer systems -- and Boeing's failure to adequately train and warn of those defects -- resulted in the crash.
The lawyers could not immediately say whether the amount of the damages being sought is being disclosed.
AeroPeru Flight 603, which left New York City bound for Santiago, Chile, via Miami and Lima, Peru, started experiencing trouble when it took off from Lima.

According to the suit, the aircraft's flight instruments and flight management computer systems began giving conflicting and erroneous information, warnings and alarms to the flight crew, and the computer system also sent erroneous information back to the control tower in Lima.
The confusion continued for 29 minutes as the captain attempted to bring the aircraft back to Lima. The plane crashed after one of its engines failed.

According to the plaintiffs' lawyer of the Miami law firm of Colson, Hicks, Eidson, Colson, Matthews, Martinez and Mendoza, the crash of a Birgenair 757 off the coast of the Dominican Repuplic less than eight months earlier, showed "striking similarities" to the Aeroperu crash. The lawyer said he believes that had Boeing taken "reasonable steps" to address the problems which caused the Birgenair crash, the AeroPeru disaster may have been avoided. Officials at Boeing could not immediately be reached for comment.
